name: FK Bodø/Glimt

ucl_2026_27.qualified_via: Eliteserien 2025 runner-up; entered via qualifying rounds (path/opponents not verified)

identity.playing_style: Knutsen's Bodø/Glimt have played the same relational 4-3-3 since 2018: high defensive line, counter-pressing, short passing through the thirds and overloads around the wingers and attacking full-backs. The artificial pitch and Arctic conditions at Aspmyra are a deliberate home advantage. In 2025/26 they beat Atlético away, knocked out Inter 5-2 on aggregate in the knockout play-off and led Sporting 3-0 before losing 3-5 on aggregate in the round of 16.
principles: develop Norwegian/Scandinavian talent and sell to bigger leagues
identity.club_character: Small-town club (Bodø ~50k inhabitants) with community ownership feel; extraordinary rise from second tier (2017) to Champions League round of 16; low external pressure, high internal standards; national media darling.
identity.ownership: Member-owned Norwegian sports club (idrettslag) with a commercial subsidiary; no external majority owner
identity.political_and_social_context: Publicly documented: the club plays on artificial turf at Aspmyra, a recurring subject of UEFA/opponent complaints; strong public sustainability/community positioning; plans for a new stadium have been publicly discussed. No institution-level controversies verified for 2025/26.
identity.wage_structure: flat relative to European peers; Norwegian tax/wage levels; European prize money has raised budget substantially
identity.transfer_policy: sell one or two key players per window to major leagues; replace from Norwegian/Scandinavian market; long contracts for core players

last_season_2025_26.ucl_result: Round of 16 (beat Inter 5-2 agg. in knockout play-off; lost 3-5 agg. to Sporting CP)

strengths: Continuity: Knutsen (since 2018, contracted to 2029) and an unchanged 4-3-3 give a level of tactical automatism few Pot 3 sides have.
Proven Champions League pedigree: 2025/26 round of 16, including wins over Atlético (away) and Inter (5-2 agg.).
Aspmyra artificial pitch plus Arctic winter fixtures are a documented home advantage (home opponents this season include Dortmund and Atlético).
70 Eliteserien points in 2025, one behind champions Viking, shows sustained domestic level.
weaknesses: Squad depth for a season running through the Norwegian off-season (Jan 2027 fixtures) is historically thin.
Lost the 2025 Eliteserien title on the final day by one point; 5-0 collapse in Lisbon shows vulnerability under sustained pressure.
Small budget: regular sale of key players each window means constant rebuilding (2026 departures could not be verified).
Away form against elite pressing sides is weaker than the home record.

positional_needs.profile: quick, comfortable in very high line, 21-26
positional_needs.reason: high line exposed in the 5-0 defeat at Sporting; ageing core (unverified departures)

positional_needs.profile: pressing 9 who links play, Scandinavian market
positional_needs.reason: depth behind first-choice striker for a double-competition winter

data_quality.notes: Verified: coach Knutsen (contract to 2029; Strasbourg interest reported), UCL opponents with venues (club/NRK reports), 2025 Eliteserien 2nd place with 70 pts (Viking 71), 2025/26 UCL round-of-16 exit. NOT verified: 2025 W/D/L and goals, Norwegian Cup result, top scorer, the 2026/27 qualifying path, and the entire summer-2026 window and current squad (squad left empty rather than guessed, because web access was lost before squad sources could be reached). Note the Eliteserien runs Mar-Nov, so 'last season' = 2025 calendar season.
